panels.title: KonkServices total
panels.description: Total KonkService CRs across the fleet.

panels.title: Deployments scaled to 0
panels.description: Any konk-service Deployment with replicas=0. A scaled-to-0 kubeconfig Deployment silently expires the client cert within 12h.

panels.title: Deployments with 0 available
panels.description: kubeconfig or apiservice Deployments with no available replica.

panels.title: Worst kubeconfig cert (h)
panels.description: Shortest remaining kubeconfig client cert in the fleet. 12h TTL, so under 2h is critical.

panels.title: Backends with no endpoints
panels.description: APIService backends with zero ready endpoints — the backend is completely down. On newer kube-state-metrics this metric is replaced by kube_endpoint_address{ready="true"}; see the panel query if this reads 0 unexpectedly.

panels.title: Pods not Ready by component
panels.description: konk-service pods failing readiness, split by component. Uses pod-name suffixes because kube-state-metrics does not expose app.kubernetes.io/component.

panels.title: ⚠ kubeconfig Deployment scaled to 0
panels.description: HIGHEST-VALUE PANEL. A scaled-to-0 kubeconfig Deployment stops cert renewal and the 12h client cert expires with no other warning. Alert immediately on any row.

panels.title: Deployment desired vs available
panels.description: Desired vs available replicas per Deployment. available < desired means the component is degraded.

panels.title: Unavailable replicas over time
panels.description: Shows how long a component has been degraded, not just that it is degraded now.

targets.expr: count by (namespace) (resource_created_at_seconds{group="konk.infoblox.com",kind="KonkService", namespace=~"$namespace"}) - on(namespace) (count by (namespace) (kube_deployment_spec_replicas{namespace=~"$namespace", deployment=~".*-kubeconfig"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: Missing component Deployments
panels.description: KonkService count minus kubeconfig-Deployment count, per namespace. Any non-zero value means a KonkService is missing a required Deployment.

panels.title: ★ apiservice-test readiness (ground truth)
panels.description: GROUND TRUTH. This probe passes only when the APIService exists and its API group lists resources inside konk. If this is red the API is not serving, whatever the other panels say.

panels.title: kubeconfig pod readiness
panels.description: Not Ready for more than 12h means the client cert has already expired.

panels.title: apiservice pod readiness
panels.description: Covers both the v1 (kubectl-apiservice) and v2 (konk-service-apiservice) names.

panels.title: Restarts (24h) by pod
panels.description: These pods should run continuously since creation, so any restart is worth a look.

panels.title: Readiness flapping (6h transitions)
panels.description: Metric-native equivalent of the e2e script's 'recently recovered' warning. More than 2 transitions in 6h means flapping, which distinguishes a transient blip from sustained instability.

panels.title: Pod age
panels.description: A young pod that is Ready indicates a recent recovery — worth finding out why it restarted.

panels.title: ★ kubeconfig cert remaining (hours)
panels.description: 12h TTL, renewed by the kubeconfig Deployment's 30s loop. Under 2h is critical, under 4h is a warning.

panels.title: Server cert remaining (days)
panels.description: ~90 day TTL, issued by cert-manager. The e2e script warns below 7 days.

panels.title: Certificates not Ready
panels.description: Any row is a Certificate cert-manager could not issue. Alert on any.

panels.title: Cert renewal activity (24h)
panels.description: A 12h cert should re-issue roughly twice a day. Zero changes over 24h means the renewal loop is stuck even though the pod may look Ready.

panels.title: ★ CA rotated without propagation
panels.description: Highest-value alert in the spec. Catches the us-dev-5 outage: the CA rotated but the per-namespace kubeconfig certs were never re-issued. Fires ~20 min BEFORE pods start failing TLS, so it is a warning rather than a post-mortem.

panels.title: ★ Backends with no ready endpoints
panels.description: The e2e script's harshest failure: the APIService backend is completely down. Alert on any row. kube-state-metrics version note: newer KSM replaces kube_endpoint_address_available with kube_endpoint_address{ready="true"}. If this panel is empty, switch to sum by (namespace, endpoint) (kube_endpoint_address{ready="true"}).

panels.title: Ready endpoint count per backend
panels.description: Watch for drops to 0. kube-state-metrics version note: newer KSM replaces kube_endpoint_address_available with kube_endpoint_address{ready="true"}. If this panel is empty, switch to sum by (namespace, endpoint) (kube_endpoint_address{ready="true"}).

panels.title: Endpoints metric absent
panels.description: Fires when the selection returns no endpoint series at all — either no Endpoints objects exist, or this KSM version uses the newer metric name. Note: absent() cannot detect a single missing service, only a wholly empty result. kube-state-metrics version note: newer KSM replaces kube_endpoint_address_available with kube_endpoint_address{ready="true"}. If this panel is empty, switch to sum by (namespace, endpoint) (kube_endpoint_address{ready="true"}).

panels.title: Backend pod readiness
panels.description: Broad view of every pod in the KonkService namespaces — these are the pods actually serving the aggregated APIs.

panels.title: CPU usage
panels.description: Per-pod CPU with the configured request overlaid as a reference line.

panels.title: Memory usage
panels.description: Working set, not usage_bytes: working set is what the OOM killer evaluates, while usage_bytes includes reclaimable page cache and reads alarmingly high.

panels.title: CPU throttling
panels.description: Sustained throttling means the CPU limit is too low for the 30s reconcile loops.

panels.title: Memory usage vs limit %
panels.description: The panel worth alerting on, more than raw bytes. Empty if no memory limits are set on the containers.

panels.title: Peak memory over window
panels.description: Highest working set over the selected time range, worst first — use it for sizing.

panels.title: ★ OOMKills
panels.description: Pair this with Row 3. These are 30s reconcile loops, so a silent OOMKill shows up there only as an unexplained restart — this panel supplies the reason.
